description: One context request to one result. CLI resolves project/service and observes facts. Daemon identity_gate verifies facts and owns identity selection, creation, recovery, registration through the existing host transaction, default lease and full project snapshot. Identity recovery is the anchor ladder in docs/design/collab-anchor-restore-model.md: a caller presenting one designed anchor is resolvable with no further fields (tmux owned pane, dsh session anchor, or a complete AppServer observation set), matched against a persisted anchor value with no liveness probe, runtime state or generation requirement; a no-match anchor drafts a new identity; ambiguity or a cross-project match stays an explicit fail-closed terminal that neither this path nor any recovery entry overrides, so a human adjudicates it; master authority is a separate flow in docs/dagpipe/collab-master-authority.graph.json. This revision makes the daemon evict a conflicting pane claim by default: a tmux pane is one owned resource host-wide, so a later registration on the pane address wins it, and a stale host route index entry (one that references a route, runtime or binding the project runtime no longer has) is unusable recovery evidence rather than a fatal error, so the write path republishes this binding's own route and the host index evicts the stale claimant in that same route commit. Only that stale-index class is tolerated: a genuine index/runtime conflict, an App Server identity-verification failure, unknown liveness, a retired address and an ambiguous address all stay explicit errors with a non-zero exit. The credential guard in the same node also skips recovery only when a committed local credential (one that carries a runtime) already exists: an incomplete local draft is not a credential, so the daemon recovers the committed token for the proven anchor from the reducer instead of presenting the draft token, while a draft that has no committed record for that anchor keeps its token unchanged. The caller therefore never probes identity, route or archives. Missing facts and explicit failures are invocation-local result terminals inside this stage; no pending workflow. A --provide supplement containing only absent session_id/thread_id/endpoint/namespace starts a new invocation, never a backward edge. No worker selection or CLI recovery sequence. Existing authenticated commands retain their admission; host-local bootstrap uses the existing 0600 Unix socket and verifies actual endpoints before mint. Exact schemas, admission, credentials, commit/lost-response and cleanup contracts: docs/design/collab-identity-minimal-interaction.md, docs/design/collab-anchor-restore-model.md and docs/design/collab-identity-shortest-path.md. Local env is diagnostic observation only; snapshot strips internal credential receipt.
